title: Flow through five nozzle designs
intro:
Five spray-nozzle designs (A to E) were each tested five times and the flow rate measured (L/min). The ANOVA rejects equal means. Which designs differ? Use Tukey's HSD at α = 0.05.

Find the Tukey critical value q and how many of the 10 pairs differ. (On the way, work out the honestly significant difference HSD = q × √(MS within / n).) Give q to three decimals; the number of pairs is a whole number.

To use the Workbench: press **Copy the data**, press Ctrl+B, click **+ Data table** and paste (Ctrl+V). Choose **One-way ANOVA** in the list on the left, set **Data table** to the table you pasted, **Layout** to *Each column is a group*, leave **Group columns** blank and set **Significance level (α)** to 0.05. Ctrl+L brings you back.

TukeySignificant.says: That is how many pairs plain two-sample t-tests at α = 0.05 call different. With 10 comparisons that inflates the familywise error. Compare each difference of means with Tukey's HSD instead.
That is the Bonferroni count (each t-test at α/10 = 0.005). Bonferroni is valid but more conservative than Tukey for all pairs; the exercise asks Tukey's HSD.
Not every pair differs. A significant F says at least one mean differs; compare each |ȳᵢ − ȳⱼ| with the HSD.

hints: There are k = 5 groups and N − k = 25 − 5 = 20 within-groups df. q comes from the studentized range distribution: Python stats.studentized_range.ppf(0.95, 5, 20), R qtukey(0.95, 5, 20).
HSD = q × √(MS within / n) with n = 5 per group. Any two means further apart than the HSD differ.
Write the five means in order and check each of the 10 differences against the HSD.
